newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, forwards ease further.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, forwards ease further.

text.p: The Indian rupee appreciated against the dollar on lack of demand for the US currency closing Wednesday at 35.83/84 against the day's opening quotes of 35.87/88, dealers said.
They said the rupee gained on good supply of dollars and poor demand.

"The rupee was on a one-way street today," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "It strengthened as there was little demand from an east Indian state-run bank which normally determines the market movement."
Dealers said most of the trade on Wednesday appeared to be inter-bank deals.
"Some banks seemed to be squaring off their positions," said a dealer. "We did not see much selling from exporters."

Dealers said the rupee appreciated against the forward dollar on continued intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). They said the RBI rolled over December maturity swaps and its receiving of premia helped the rupee to appreciate.
Dealers said the RBI has been active in rolling over swaps since last week.
"The RBI was receiving December over May and December over June," said a dealer. "Forwards are likely to remain soft for some more time to come."
The six-month premia for forward dollars ended Wednesday at an annualised 7.08 percent against the day's opening 7.41 percent and Monday's close of 7.47 percent.
